newsitem.title: UK: Thames Water wins Jakarta water supply deal.
newsitem.headline: Thames Water wins Jakarta water supply deal.

text.p: British utility Thames Water Plc said on Friday it and Indonesia's PT Kekarpola Airindo had won a 25-year contract to supply water to eastern Jakarta.

Thames, as majority shareholder in the consortium, said the project would be financed 30 percent by equity and 70 percent by borrowing. Thames would invest up to 70 percent of the equity, amounting to around $72 million.
The company said the deal would enable around 3.5 million people to receive piped water in the first five years. At present, two million have piped water in the city.
Thames said the concession was expected to have average annual turnover of $92 million in the first five years, rising to more than $200 million annually later.
The consortium was expected to invest around $260 million in the first five years and begin supplying water in early 1998.
The concession to supply the western half of the city was expected to be won by another consortium, Thames said.
